subject: PilotFrame LangChain Trace + PromptOps integration — sandbox acceptance & MAP
messages:
From: Aliza Patel <aliza@pilotframe.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: tom@pilotframe.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: PilotFrame → Redwood: LangChain + PromptOps integration — sandbox proposal

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked promising. We’d like to move forward with a scoped pilot: embed PilotFrame’s PromptOps layer into Redwood-hosted LangChain runtime so we can collect prompt telemetry and token-attribution traces for our Knowledge Retrieval pipeline.

High-level ask:
- Sandbox with Redwood-hosted LangChain endpoint (non-prod) for 30 days
- Tracing hooks for token attribution and prompt versioning (we can add an SDK shim on our side)
- Acceptance criteria: trace events for >95% of requests, sample export to our telemetry, and no PII leakage in traces

Tom (cc) will be the technical lead. Can you share a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) and an initial acceptance checklist? We can do a short kick-off next week.

Thanks,
Aliza Patel
Head of Integrations | PilotFrame
[Attachment: PilotFrame_IntroDeck.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Aliza Patel <aliza@pilotframe.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom@pilotframe.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PilotFrame → Redwood: LangChain + PromptOps integration — sandbox proposal

Aliza — thanks, excited to run this with you. Attached is a short integration quickstart and a sandbox acceptance checklist draft. Proposed MAP (high level):

1) Week 0: Kick-off + access provisioning (sandbox creds, IP allowlists)
2) Week 1: Tracing shim install + smoke tests (sample events)
3) Week 2: Throughput test & stability (500 rps bursts in sandbox)
4) Week 3: Acceptance run (10k requests, verify trace coverage & PII redaction)
5) Week 4: Review results, agree on next steps (Dedicated eval or co-build)

Security/compliance notes: we’ll enable redwood’s token-level redaction and can route sandbox traffic to a dedicated, ephemeral model instance so no data mixes with production. Please confirm the telemetry retention window you need.

I’ve looped in Vanessa for commercial and Marissa for SDK/interop support. Proposed kickoff: Tue Apr 13 09:00 PT — does that work?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-integration-quickstart.md (MD, 8KB)]
From: Tom Reynolds <tom@pilotframe.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: Aliza Patel <aliza@pilotframe.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PilotFrame → Redwood: LangChain + PromptOps integration — sandbox proposal

Thanks Stephanie — Tue 09:00 PT works for our team. A couple of technical clarifications before kick-off so we can prep: 

1) Trace format: PilotFrame expects per-token attribution with a trace_id and prompt_version metadata. Is Redwood able to emit a trace envelope that includes model_name, model_revision, request_id, and per-token source metadata?

2) Sampling: we intend to sample 10% of production-equivalent traffic. For sandbox, can we enable deterministic sampling (seeded) so our side can validate replayed sequences?

3) PII redaction: we need to confirm which fields Redwood redacts automatically vs. which we should scrub on our SDK side. We will not send phone numbers in test data but want to confirm redaction markers appear in trace export.

Jonas (cc) is our runtime engineer for the LangChain adapter — Jonas, could you propose the shim approach (pre/post-token hooks vs. runtime patch)?

- Tom
VP Engineering | PilotFrame
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@pilotframe.ai>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PilotFrame → Redwood: LangChain + PromptOps integration — sandbox proposal

Tom — good questions. Quick answers and plan: 

- Trace envelope: Yes. Redwood can emit an envelope per request containing model_name, model_revision, request_id, timestamp, and an event array. We can extend the event array to include per-token attribution fields (source_id, prompt_version).

- Hooks vs patch: For LangChain runtime the least invasive is a small tracer shim that wraps the LangChain LLM invoke and annotates tokens as they are produced (pre-token hook). I’ve attached a prototype patch and a small acceptance checklist we use internally.

- Sampling: Sandbox supports deterministic sampling via a seed param on the trace exporter. We’ll expose that on the sandbox config UI and via the API.

- PII redaction: Redwood will mark redacted spans with [REDACTED] and include a redaction_reason code. We recommend PilotFrame avoid sending raw PII in the pilot but we will show redaction behavior in the acceptance report.

Next steps:
- I’ll push the trace-hook prototype to the sandbox cluster today (branch: pf-trace-shim).
- Stephanie/Marissa: please share the sandbox creds and the acceptance checklist with the PilotFrame team before the Tue call.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: trace-hook-patch.diff (PATCH, 4KB)]
